Ok. Wall of text. Be prepared.

So when you start brushing your hair, start from the ends. Detangle one inch at a time. If you start at the top and brush down, you'll rip parts of the tangles, causing broken hairs (ie flyaways). You'll still have some flyaways from newly-grown hair, but they'll be easily controllable with a bit of hairspray, versus having an unintentional mullet. IF you already have them, it'll take a good two months or so for them to start to disappear as they grow out, so patience.

Hot oil treatments are my FAVORITE thing. They make hair so soft and lovely. I did mine once-weekly in the winter, and twice-weekly in the summer, depending on how much time I spent outside in the blistering sun. V05 Hot Oil Therapy is the best for my (curly, medium-thick) hair. Basically after washing and conditioning hair like normal, you let the warmed oil soak into your hair for a minute or so, then rinse it (or something, I've had short hair for a year so I forget the exact directions. They're on the box).

For the very tippy-roots (and only during the summer or as I near a trimming) I use Silkysexyhair's leave-in conditioner. Just for the bottom two-four inches though (where split ends happen), because this stuff is EXTREMELY greasy. You'll look unshowered if you use too much.

Finally, DO NOT USE SULFATED shampoos. They'll dry you out and you'll be crackly and dull. Find something (shampoo and conditioner both) that have no sulfates or alcohols. Organix is good, but some of their scents have sulfates. Ology from walgreens is good, but they get recalled for misprints a lot too.

BTW these are all drug-store fixes, because I'm poor. If you have something that fits along these lines from a salon that works better for your hair-type, go for it.
